messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — gpu-pool queue depth high (us-west2-preemptible). Rule: gpu.pool.queue_depth > 200 for 5m. Significant Pending pods due to InsufficientResources (PreemptibleGPU). Potential multi-zone eviction waterfall. Auto-created thread 3098765432

maria: I’m the oncall, ack. Pulling up autoscaler and scheduler events now. Priya, can you grab the metrics (queue length, pod pending) and any recent preemption spikes?

ashley: looking at cluster events — huge spike of NodeReclaimed events across us-west2-a/b. Feels like a batch reclaim that hit our spot pools. Example from kube-events:
```
Apr 23 14:07:12 node-uw2-a kubelet: NodeReclaimed: instance preempted by cloud provider
Apr 23 14:07:14 node-uw2-b kubelet: NodeReclaimed: instance preempted by cloud provider
```
Pod pending count for inference namespace: 342 -> many are WaitingForGPU.

priya: Metrics snapshot: gpu.queue_depth = 312 (5m avg), avg token throughput dipped 28%, 95th latency for /generate jumped from 380ms -> 1.9s. Error surface: 429s and some 503s from backend fallback. Customers affected: two high-volume customers reported elevated 429s (ingestion spikes). Posting Grafana links: <https://grafana/redwood/d/q123/gpu-pool|queue/hosts>

sam: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up attempts but failing with capacity errors and then hitting pool.max_pools limit. Key line: "scale failed: no suitable instance types; preemptible quota exhausted; maxPools=5 reached". Also seeing rapid scale down after partial fills -> autoscaler thrash.

maria: So it's a multi-zone preemption cascade -> capacity backfill can't keep up -> autoscaler hits maxPools -> queue grows -> throttling. OK. First mitigations: 1) reduce shedding threshold to avoid cascading client retries 2) open fallback to dedicated pool for critical traffic 3) disable aggressive scale-down policy temporarily to avoid thrash.

ashley: I’ll run quick kube commands to list pending pods + describe one failing pod:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide | grep gpu | wc -l
# => 312
kubectl -n inference describe pod inference-gen-77c9f | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Describe shows: "0/0 nodes available: Insufficient gpu, Insufficient memory" and tolerations ok.

priya: I’m updating the routing policy now to divert a slice of traffic to dedicated-gpu-reserve. Will send 30% of traffic for /generate and /chat to dedicated for the next 45m. Patch command: `redwoodctl routing set --route /generate --fallback dedicated-gpu-reserve --weight 0.3 --ttl 2700`

sam: Applying autoscaler tweak: bump maxPools from 5 -> 8 and set scaleDownCooldown to 10m. Command: `kubectl patch configmap gpu-autoscaler -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"maxPools":"8","scaleDownCooldown":"600"}}'`

infra-sre-bot: Deploy accepted. GPUs reserved in dedicated pool via Dedicated API: reservation_id=ded-20260423-23. Estimated spinup time 6m.

maria: Good. Also enable prefix cache warmup to reduce cold-KV misses that amplify token compute. Priya can you trigger a small warmup job across existing warm candidates?

priya: Warmup job queued: `kubectl -n infra run cache-warmup --image=redwood/cache-warmup:stable --replicas=10 -- /warm --targets=hot-model-shards`

ashley: Noting customer impact in incident notes: elevated latency and ~1.2% 429 rate for tenant-red-1 and tenant-alpha. CS prep: notify top 5 affected customers with mitigation in progress.

maria: Oncall handoff: @sam you’re primary for autoscaler config and cluster-level changes. @ashley you own the node/pool mitigation and logs. Priya you own routing and customer comms. I’ll run the incident and coordinate postmortem.

sam: Confirmed patch applied to autoscaler, and we’re seeing new nodes provisioning into dedicated-reserve. New node events starting at 14:13 UTC. Monitoring pool_utilization, will post updates.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0423 — Sev: high — channels: #incidents, #eng-runtime, #support. Pageresponse required.

ashley: After routing and autoscaler changes, queue_depth dropped from 312 -> 78 in 8 minutes. Error rate on /generate down to 0.15%. Rolling restart avoided.

priya: Customer comms drafts: "We experienced degraded inference capacity due to a preemptible GPU reclaim in us-west2 causing autoscaler limits. We’ve diverted traffic to dedicated capacity and adjusted autoscaler settings. We expect normal performance within 30-45 minutes. We’re investigating long-term mitigation." Posting to CS now.

maria: Good progress. Next steps: 1) keep dedicated fallback active for 30-60m, 2) follow up on quota/preemptible allocation with cloud provider, 3) lower autoscaler sensitivity to spot loss (increase stabilization), 4) add warning to runbook about multi-zone reclaim waterfall and maxPools knob. Assignments: Sam -> cloud quota request + autoscaler permanence; Ashley -> runbook + node pool health checks; Priya -> customer postmortem note.

sam: Filing cloud support ticket SR-67412 requesting more preemptible capacity and checking recent reclaim cause. ETA from provider unknown.

infra-sre-bot: Metric alert cleared (gpu.pool.queue_depth back under threshold).

maria: Closing live mitigation. We’ll do a formal postmortem and link to this thread. One action item: add a cron that pre-warms prefix cache during expected reclaim windows.

ashley: Noted, will add to runbook and file a follow-up ticket INT-2026-0042.

priya: Thanks team. Leaving routing fallback active for 1h and will reduce if stable. Marking thread resolved for now.

maria: Thanks all — good coordination. Postmortem owners: maria (incident lead), ashley (runbook author), sam (autoscaler follow-up), priya (customer comms). Closing thread at 3098765899.
